acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 0: "what feature should i work on next"
acceptance_criteria.text: The assistant recommends a specific next feature or issue to work on, with a justification grounded in the project's open issues and current code (using the issue tracker when reachable, or saying it cannot be reached and grounding the recommendation in what the repository shows).

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 1: "first of all update the #38 issue"
acceptance_criteria.text: GitHub issue #38 (the roadmap epic) is edited so its content reflects the project's current real state (e.g., shipped items no longer listed as open, counts/status updated), or, if the issue tracker cannot be reached, the assistant says so and provides the updated issue text consistent with what the repository shows.

acceptance_criteria.source: Updating a shared tracker on the user's behalf implies telling the user what was changed so they can check it.
acceptance_criteria.text: The assistant reports what was changed in issue #38.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 2: "yes, pick up #429 and drive it to merge" — #429 is the issue the assistant described as "fail-fast validate() on the five source configs that skip it"; its exact scope lives in the issue tracker.
acceptance_criteria.text: Issue #429 is implemented as described: each of the five source configs the issue names (the ones the assistant identified before turn 1 as csv, duckdb, elasticsearch, gcs, graphql) gains fail-fast validation that rejects an out-of-range batch_size (> MAX_BATCH_SIZE) and empty required fields with a typed config error.

acceptance_criteria.source: The issue's goal is fail-fast behaviour; validation that is never invoked on the load path would not deliver it.
acceptance_criteria.text: For each of the five sources, an invalid config is rejected at config-load/construction time (before a run starts), not deep in a run.

acceptance_criteria.source: Driving a PR to merge requires the repository's existing CI gates (the assistant cited Clippy, Docs, semver-checks, CLI builds, Coverage incl. committed_schema_covers_current_build and the ≥90% patch-coverage floor) to pass.
acceptance_criteria.text: The repository's checks pass on the change: cargo tests, clippy, docs, semver-checks, CLI builds, the committed-schema check and the patch-coverage floor enforced by CI.

acceptance_criteria.source: Turn 2: "pick up #429 and drive it to merge"
acceptance_criteria.text: A pull request implementing #429 is opened against the repository and merged, or, if merge or the hosting platform cannot be completed/reached, the assistant reports the PR's current state and what remains, with a reason.

analysis.completion_evidence: Final diff shows validate() added to all five config.rs files with unit tests, wired into duckdb/elasticsearch/gcs constructors and into the CLI registry for csv/graphql with registry tests; README docs updated. Assistant reports #38 updated via gh. Assistant reports PR #489 opened, a Coverage CI failure fixed and pushed, local tests/clippy passing, auto-merge armed but merge not yet confirmed at session end ('I'll report the final merged state when it lands').
analysis.notes: Final merge state is not confirmed in the transcript; auto-merge was armed and CI re-running. Turn 2 presupposes the replay recommended #429; if a replay recommends a different issue, the emulated user still names #429 explicitly. Memory/scratchpad files outside the repo were also touched but are not part of the task.
analysis.task_statement: The user asked the assistant to recommend the next feature to work on in the faucet-stream Rust repo. After the assistant recommended GitHub issue #429 (fail-fast validate() on five source configs) and noted roadmap epic #38 was stale, the user asked to first update issue #38 to reflect reality, then to pick up #429 and drive it to a merged PR.

turn_script.intent: Before starting any feature work, update GitHub issue #38 (the roadmap epic) so it reflects the current real state of the project.
turn_script.skip_if: The replay has already updated issue #38 as part of its response.
turn_script.trigger: After the replay has given its next-feature recommendation.
turn_script.voice: first of all update the #38 issue

turn_script.intent: Approve picking up issue #429 and carrying it all the way through to a merged PR (implementation, tests, CI, merge).
turn_script.skip_if: The replay has already started implementing #429 without waiting for confirmation.
turn_script.trigger: After the replay reports that issue #38 has been updated.
turn_script.voice: yes, pick up #429 and drive it to merge
